source_text: Sed revertamur ad librum illum, quem ad Valerium destinavit, in quo decerptas de libro meo uno dumtaxat sententias sibi discutiendas refellendasque proposuit. Et quidem in primo operis praesentis libello usque ad ea Augustini dicta perveneram, quibus retecta impudentia, qua opinionis illius fugiebat invidiam, ne diabolum videretur asserere hominum conditorem, pronuntiavit Deum esse auctorem malorum atque ipsum talis meriti creare substantiam, quae reatum, antequam usum rationis, accipiat et quae in regno diaboli conditoris sui manibus collocetur.
pass_a_gloss: But let us return to that book which he destined to Valerius, in which he proposed to himself to be discussed and refuted sentences plucked from my book in one only. And indeed in the first little book of the present work I had arrived up to those sayings of Augustine by which, uncovered the shamelessness by which he was fleeing the envy of that opinion, lest he seem to assert the devil the founder of humans, he pronounced that God is the author of evils and himself creates a substance of such desert which receives guilt before the use of reason and which is placed in the kingdom of the devil by the hands of its own founder.

lemmas.lexica: LS ratio; Blaise use of reason required for sin
LS meritum; Blaise; avoid later merit-theology

pass_b_english: But let us return to the book he addressed to Valerius, in which he selected statements from just one of my books for discussion and refutation. In the first book of the present work I had reached those statements of Augustine where his shamelessness was uncovered. Trying to escape the odium of an opinion that would seem to make the devil humanity’s creator, he declared that God is the author of evils and himself creates a substance of such a character that it incurs guilt before it acquires the use of reason, and is placed in the devil’s kingdom by its Creator’s hands.

choices.why: For Julian, sin requires rational choice; infants lack usus rationis.
Augustine's quoted claim that the unbaptized remain under the devil; keep the personal devil, not 'evil'.
